newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end sharply up on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end sharply up on fund buying.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed sharply higher on Thursday as domestic mutual funds and foreign financial institutions made selective purchases, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index ended 17.72 points, or 2.16 percent, higher at 838.14 points.
Brokers said purchases by leading domestic financial institution Unit Trust of India also helped fuel the rally in share prices.
"Revival of buying by general investors, though selective, was another significant factor which aided the rising trend," said one broker.

"Rumours that B.A.T, a major shareholder in ITC, might enhance its controlling stake in the company also fuelled speculative buying in the market," said S.C. Juneja of brokers Jaico Credit Investments.
Britain's BAT Industries Plc holds a 31.7 percent stake in ITC.
ITC surged 27.25 rupees, or 5.52 percent, to 520.60 on heavy speculative buying, brokers said.
Hindustan Lever shot up 48 rupees to 1,288.
Nestle India ended 5.50 rupees higher at 279.50 on buying by foreign investors, they said.
Larsen and Toubro climbed 7.45 rupees to 235.90.
